title: süt and fúj: What the Sun and Wind Do

sections.title: Verb-first weather sentences
sections.content: Hungarian describes the sun and the wind with their own verbs, and the subject comes after the verb: Süt a nap. ("The sun is shining", literally "shines the sun") and Fúj a szél. ("The wind is blowing"). This verb-first order is normal for weather sentences — don't try to move nap or szél to the front.

items.spanish: Ma egész nap süt a nap.
items.english: The sun is shining all day today.

items.spanish: Nem süt a nap, felhős az ég.
items.english: The sun isn't shining, the sky is cloudy.

sections.content: nap means both "day" and "sun" — you already know it as "day". Context always makes it clear which one is meant: egy nap ("a day") vs. süt a nap ("the sun shines").
